description: Pairs of requests that are semantically DIFFERENT and MUST produce distinct cache keys. Every one of these would be wrongly merged by a naive normalizer.

pairs.why: Credentials are case-sensitive. A raw policy must never lowercase values; 'Bearer ABC' != 'Bearer abc'.
Accept uses order as preference. token_list preserves order; only true sets (Accept-Encoding) use token_set.
Only the media type is case-folded; parameter bytes are preserved, so utf-8 != utf-16.
Case-folding applies to bare RFC tokens only. Text inside quoted-strings is opaque: "Hello" != "hello".
A request sending Accept-Encoding: gzip differs from one sending no Accept-Encoding at all.
An empty field line is still a field (0 elements vs absent); the length-framed encoding keeps them apart.
token_set ignores order/duplicates but never membership: one coding vs two codings stay distinct.
Two raw field lines 'a' then 'b' merge to a,b and must never collide with one line whose value is the literal "a,b".
One quoted element "gzip, deflate" is a different request from two elements gzip / deflate. Naive comma-splitting merges them.
application/json and application/xml are different representations.
